Issued at 1230 AM CDT Thu Aug 13 2026

This Morning: MCS Potential

An MCS taking shape across Nebraska will continue propagating 
eastward this morning as a 500hPa shortwave trough traverses nearly 
zonal flow across the central to eastern United States. Expectations 
are for this MCS and its associated impacts to remain south of our 
area, generally along and south of the I-80 corridor as higher 
dewpoints and instability reside over these areas, south of a 
surface boundary situated across northern Iowa. That said, some 
shower and storm activity is possible across northeast 
Iowa/southwest Wisconsin during the morning hours (60-80%) as the 
upper wave moves through the region. If the MCS were to track 
further northward, those south of Highway 18 would see some 
potential for a stronger wind gusts given DCAPE values of 500-1000 
J/kg, PWATs around 1.6in, and 0-3km shear of 20-30kts oriented 
nearly perpendicular to the MCS per the 13.03z RAP, though this a 
low probability scenario (< 10%) given the more favorable 
environment will exist south of our area. 

Outside of the low MCS potential, patchy fog has begun to develop 
across southwest Wisconsin which may extend into northeast Iowa. 
However, increasing cloud cover overnight will act to limit the 
amount of radiational cooling across the region and the western 
extent of fog development. Fog will begin to dissipate through the 
morning hours. 

This Afternoon - Friday Morning: Showers and Storms, Heavy Rainfall

Some uncertainty exists regarding how the rest of today will play 
out after the MCS moves out of the area. Remnant outflow and 
differential heating boundaries associated with the morning 
convection look to set-up across portions of the Upper Mississippi 
River Valley, though where exactly these situate themselves is 
tricky to pinpoint. Mid-level PVA is also depicted in the 
deterministic models which would provide synoptic-scale ascent atop 
the various surface boundaries. Another point of uncertainty 
regarding storm development during the afternoon is the influence of 
cloud coverage from the morning convection and how much instability 
develops in the afternoon. 13.00z model soundings do suggest that 
MUCAPE on the order of 700-1000 J/kg develops this afternoon, 
primarily focused across the Minnesota/Iowa border and into far 
southwest Wisconsin which would support convective initiation given 
the forcing mechanisms in place. If storms develop, they would 
likely remain sub-severe given the weak instability though some 
elongation in the hodographs suggests a stronger updraft can't be 
ruled out. 

Late tonight, a strengthening 850hPa low level jet and associated 
moisture transport noses into the surface boundary across Iowa, 
providing a source of lift for convective development through Friday 
morning. Within this region of ascent, mid to upper 60s dewpoints 
will be in place along with PWATs of 1.8-2in, warm cloud depths in 
excess of 10kft, and MUCAPE values of 1000-1250 J/kg. Cloud layer 
winds also look to be nearly boundary parallel per the 13.03z RAP 
which would suggest some training of storms is also possible. These 
parameters indicate the environment will be primed for heavy 
rainfall along the boundary as we head into Friday morning. 

Where exactly the boundary will reside is somewhat uncertain given 
the overnight time period and rainfall cooling the atmosphere ahead 
of the boundary though expectations would favor a southern solution 
given this conceptual model. Most of the CAM solutions including the 
13.00z HREF/REFS indicate the boundary will primarily remain to the 
south of our area, along with the axis of heaviest rainfall, which 
fits said conceptual model. As such, probabilities for 1 inch or 
more of rain are highest across central into east-central Iowa with 
only a 10-30% chance for those south of Highway 18 in our area. 
Given these current expectations, flooding potential looks to 
largely remain south of our area though if a northward trend begins 
to develop localized flooding may become more of a concern. This 
appears to be an unlikely scenario though as there has been a 
southward trend in the 13.00z REFS. 

Saturday - Tuesday: Periodic Showers and Storms

With zonal flow remaining situated over the central United States, 
several mid to upper level shortwaves will have the opportunity to 
traverse the Upper Midwest through the weekend. Each of these waves 
brings the potential for showers and storms, primarily early 
Saturday morning (60-80%) and Saturday night into Sunday morning (40-
60%). There's quite a bit of uncertainty with how these waves 
evolve, so will need to monitor for potential impacts over the next 
few days though the overall severe threat is low at this time. 

Apart from the periodic shower/storm chances, slightly cooler 
temperatures in the upper 70s to low 80s are expected into the 
beginning of the new week with drier conditions possible as high
